olivia (support): FYI pasted ACME's report — their daily CSV export and the Console daily tile disagree. CSV stops at 2024-11-03T16:00:00Z and the chart shows totals that match a day boundary at 16:00 UTC. customer says their org timezone is America/Los_Angeles so day should end at 00:00 PST not 16:00 UTC.

samir (eng): Is this only for CSV exports or are the per-route tiles also affected?

olivia (support): Both. They attached the CSV (snippet below) and sent a screenshot of dashboard. Quote from customer: "we lost 8 hours of events on Nov 3 — totals look like they rolled over at 16:00 instead of midnight PST".

maya (analytics): Can you paste the first/last rows of the CSV and the export query we run? Might be a tz param missing.

olivia (support): CSV head: 
```
day,route_id,tokens
2024-11-02,route-123,12400
2024-11-03,route-123,5600
```
And CSV footer timestamps column (raw): 
```
2024-11-03T16:00:00Z
2024-11-04T15:59:59Z
```

samir (eng): That raw timestamp pattern (16:00Z) screams UTC truncation when a non-UTC org tz should be applied. I remember a deploy yesterday touched analytics/export. deploy-bot, any deploys to analytics around 2024-11-01..2024-11-03?

deploy-bot: Deployed rev a7c3 to prod services: analytics-export-handler and viz-tiles at 2024-11-02T09:14:22Z.

maya (analytics): I pulled the export code path. The CSV pipeline uses this SQL snippet: 
```
SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) AS day_utc, SUM(tokens) FROM usage_events WHERE org_id = $1 GROUP BY 1
```
It never applies the org timezone before truncating. The Console tiles (viz) were using moment.tz for display earlier, so charts looked like local tz, but the exported aggregation was UTC-truncated. That mismatch would make the CSV/day totals look shifted by the org tz offset.

samir (eng): Confirmed. For orgs in America/Los_Angeles, UTC truncation will shift the boundary to 16:00 UTC (00:00 PST = 08:00 UTC? wait math: PST is UTC-8, so midnight PST = 08:00 UTC, but their CSV shows 16:00 UTC which is UTC-8? Hmm double-check).

maya (analytics): Quick math: if code used date_trunc('day', ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles') but then cast back to UTC incorrectly it could flip. The exact bug: exports call date_trunc('day', ts AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') due to a default, and a recent refactor removed passing org_tz through to the DB, so everything defaults to server TZ (UTC). That makes the CSV day boundary equal to UTC midnight. For display we convert to org tz which made it look like an 8-hr gap.

olivia (support): Customer concerned about billing — they're missing daily totals on invoicing. They want a hotfix and a backfill.

samir (eng): Action items: 1) hotfix to add org_tz param to the export query and ensure date_trunc uses AT TIME ZONE org_tz, 2) run backfill job to recompute daily aggregates for affected org (ACME org_id=acme-001) for date range Nov 1-7, 3) notify customer and offer corrected CSV + explanation. I'll create a GH issue and tag urgent.

maya (analytics): Quick repro for engineers: run the SQL with/without tz: 
```
-- wrong (current prod): SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) AS day, SUM(tokens) FROM usage_events WHERE org_id = 'acme-001' GROUP BY 1;
-- correct: SELECT (date_trunc('day', ts AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles') AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AS day_utc, SUM(tokens) FROM usage_events WHERE org_id = 'acme-001' GROUP BY 1;
```
Compare counts per day, you'll see the shift.

samir (eng): I'm opening issue #INF-2346, assigning to eng-analytics, marking sev2. Will push a patch to restore passing org_tz to the export path.

olivia (support): Customer asked if this could be caused by DST transition — ACME is on Pacific and Nov 3 is near DST end in some years. Can the DST rules make the boundary wobble?

maya (analytics): DST could change exact offset hour but doesn't explain an 8-hour wholesale shift; this is a missing tz-apply problem. We'll include DST in the backfill logic (use timezone-aware functions).

samir (eng): ETA for hotfix? I can get a PR today, deploy to canary, then prod if tests pass. Expecting deploy in 6-12 hours. Backfill will run after and might take longer depending on data size; will provide an ETA in GH issue.

olivia (support): Perfect. I'll reply to ACME with temporary workaround: download JSON export and run our quick script to re-bucket by their org tz, or wait for corrected CSV. I'll also share the repro steps so they understand root cause. :+1:

maya (analytics): Leaving a note: add integration test for export tz behaviour to catch regressions.

samir (eng): Thanks — will follow up in INF-2346 with PR link and deploy details.

olivia (support): Adding this thread to the ticket and pinging customer once we have a canary with the fix.
